workflow: Background agents can hit transient API errors (socket closed, stream idle timeout) and silently recover — check on-disk output before relaunching to avoid duplicate overwrites
TaskStop fails gracefully when the process that launched the agent has already exited; orphaned agents may still complete and overwrite files
A process exit kills all in-flight background agents; re-entry requires inspecting on-disk state and applying fixes manually
Re-verification consistently surfaces additional findings the initial scan missed — plan for iteration-2 to catch residual line-range and path issues
Generated markdown files require a markdownlint pass before commit; MD040 (code fences missing language tag) is a common generated-doc violation
The two-iteration fix-loop protocol is intentional: iteration 1 clears known failures, iteration 2 handles deeper findings from the re-scan; remaining failures after cap are manual
The gsd-docs work manifest (.planning/tmp/docs-work-manifest.json) is essential for resuming after process interruption — always write it before dispatching agents

friction: Two Wave 1 agents (ARCHITECTURE, CONFIGURATION) hit transient API errors mid-run (socket closed after ~55-74 tool calls, stream idle timeout after ~370s) requiring relaunches
Original agents auto-recovered and completed while relaunched duplicates were still running, creating a race condition requiring TaskStop
All 5 iteration-2 fix agents were killed by a process exit before completing; their in-process state was lost with no partial output
TaskStop reported failure for the two orphaned Wave 1 respawns because they had died with the original process, not the current one
After process exit, Read tool state was invalidated — had to re-read files before any Edit calls would succeed
METADATA_SCHEMAS required three fix passes: 16 failures → fixer used wrong Rust file paths → 7 more failures → fixer used wrong line ranges → 5 more (manually corrected)
